title: BorgWarner to Supply Variable Turbine Geometry Turbocharger for Major European OEM’s Hybrid Electric Vehicle Platform
summary: Read and download our latest press releases.
body_text: Variable turbine geometry turbocharger will power one of the OEM’s first hybrid electric vehicle offerings in North America Technology features silencer and shot-peened compressor wheel designed to reduce noise and boost strength and durability Start of production is expected to begin in 2028 Auburn Hills, Michigan, February 11, 2026 – BorgWarner, a global product leader in delivering innovative and sustainable mobility solutions, has secured an agreement with a major European original equipment manufacturer (OEM) to supply its variable turbine geometry (VTG) turbocharger on one of its hybrid electric vehicle (HEV) platforms. This business win positions BorgWarner as part of the global supply base that will power one of the company’s first HEV offerings in North America. BorgWarner’s VTG turbocharger technology enables precise control of engine operation, optimizing performance across a broad range of engine speeds and integrating advanced combustion strategies to boost efficiency, enhance fuel economy and lower emissions. The system features adjustable, electrically-actuated vanes that regulate pressure upstream of the turbine and enable near instant acceleration and maximum power output. Tailored to meet the OEM’s size and space requirements, this customer-specific technology incorporates an updated turbine housing designed to fit the available packaging constraints and enhance transient performance. “BorgWarner is proud to extend our long-lasting, trusted partnership with this OEM by supplying our VTG technology to the company’s HEV platform,” said Dr. Volker Weng, Vice President of BorgWarner Inc. and President and General Manager, Turbos and Thermal Technologies. “Our extensive experience supplying turbochargers using our proven VTG technology for similar applications in Europe, along with our strong track record for quality and reliability, positions us well to extend our relationship and further expand our North American breadth of offerings together.” This specific turbocharger technology features a shot-peened compressor wheel designed to boost strength and durability. Through the shot-peening process, the compressor wheel gains improved resistance to wear and tear, supporting longer component life and meeting sustained performance requirements. Additionally, the compressor outlet features a silencer that helps reduce noise within the vehicle.

title: Introducing the Winnebago Sunflyer: A new era for the conventional Class C
summary: When Winnebago set out to reimagine its conventional Class C motorhome, the team rallied around a guiding principle pulled from a 1987 ad for the Minnie Winnie: “Everything in it deserves the name that’s on it.” That spirit became the North Star for the all-new Sunflyer, a modern Conventional Class C that reinvents and simplifies travel for the road ahead.
body_text: When Winnebago set out to reimagine its conventional Class C motorhome, the team rallied around a guiding principle pulled from a 1987 ad for the Minnie Winnie: “Everything in it deserves the name that’s on it.” That spirit became the North Star for the all-new Sunflyer, a modern Conventional Class C that reinvents and simplifies travel for the road ahead. “We have a duty as caretakers of the Winnebago brand to develop a product that meets our consumers’ needs and deserves the name we put on it,” said Devin A. Kasper, senior product manager at Winnebago. “That was our guiding light.” Formerly the name of a Winnebago Class A from nearly 50 years ago, Sunflyer draws on the brand’s rich legacy while also speaking to new, more accessible adventures. “It felt bright and open and connected to nature but had that legacy,” explains Kasper. “It just made sense as soon as we saw it.” The Sunflyer more than lives up to its name, with a completely redesigned base frame, an upgraded roof design reminiscent of what consumers might see in a Class A motorhome, mountain-inspired exterior graphics, and three interior colorways that feel bright and modern. What’s beneath the surface also plays a role in setting the Sunflyer apart from other conventional Class C motorhomes. The Sunflyer is equipped with an automatic generator start and a Multiplex system that allows users to control the whole coach from a touchscreen – a first for the conventional Class C segment. Advanced safety considerations were built in from the start as well, from child-seat placements and cab-over bed safety nets, to blind spot warning sideview cameras and appliances mechanically attached to the aluminum sidewall. Even the smallest additions matter: hidden door hinges, inset lighting, Pet Pal leash attachments and auxiliary solar panel plugs outside of the awning — all designed for ease of use and reflecting the attention to detail that users will certainly benefit from, even if they’re not obvious. “The best design is what you don’t really notice,” says Kasper. “It just works, and I think we’ve nailed that.” What’s even more remarkable is how it all came together. The Sunflyer was developed faster than any product in the brand’s history. The team reorganized to design multiple floor plans in parallel, shortening development by 29 weeks and bringing four floor plans to the Elkhart RV Dealer Open House last September. The project was a testament to Winnebago’s commitment to unparalleled collaboration in product development. “The only way we were able to do that was by breaking down barriers between the product team, the engineering team and the manufacturing team to work nimbly as one,” says Doug Carder, chief engineer on the Sunflyer. What began as a mission to create a new conventional Class C product became an opportunity to redefine the category itself. The Sunflyer generated strong interest from dealers and the industry when it was first unveiled and has continued to delight and impress during its recent consumer debut at the Florida RV Super Show. “We’ve really found a groove with the Sunflyer,” Kasper says. “There’s been a palpable excitement around it — not just from dealers and customers but from the teams behind the scenes who feel proud to be part of something meaningful.” The Sunflyer is just the beginning. Winnebago’s design teams are hard at work and focused on giving outdoor enthusiasts more fresh, exciting products that carry on the brand’s pioneering legacy of innovation and excellence. “Your goal is always to design the right thing, and then design that thing right,” says Kasper. “We made sure we achieved that with the Sunflyer. Just like the 1987 ad that inspired us, everything in it deserves the name that’s on it.”

body_text: Odyssey CEO Mark Gordon speaking on the Development Opportunities & Challeneges Panel at the ACCF Offshore Critical Minerals Forum on January 27, 2026. The last 72 hours have brought a wave of major policy announcements that are reshaping how the United States and its allies secure the critical minerals that power agriculture, advanced manufacturing, defense systems, and clean technologies. These developments directly align with Odyssey’s long‑term strategic vision and reinforce the relevance of Odyssey’s potential project portfolio in North America, the Cook Islands, and the U.S. Outer Continental Shelf. As an early mover with advanced, de‑risked assets, Odyssey is strongly positioned to support U.S. and allied efforts to build secure mineral supply chains. ​ They also build on the themes elevated during last week’s ACCF Critical Minerals Forum in Washington, where Odyssey participated alongside policymakers, researchers, and industry leaders to discuss the role of marine minerals in resilient critical mineral supply chains.​ ​Here’s what we’re watching — and why it matters for our work: ​ A new U.S.–Mexico Critical Minerals Action Plan introduced coordinated trade policies, regulatory cooperation, geological mapping alignment, and potential price floors for select minerals. Our phosphate projects sit squarely in the North American supply‑chain corridor now under active bilateral coordination, at a time when phosphate is recognized as a U.S. critical mineral. This aligns our work with a growing binational framework for secure fertilizer inputs and food‑system resilience. In remarks delivered at the U.S. State Department’s 2026 Critical Minerals Ministerial , Vice President Vance outlined the administration’s intent to build a multi‑nation critical minerals trading bloc. Our diversified project portfolio focused on high demand critical minerals fits directly into a future where allied‑aligned producers gain from more stable, transparent, and standards‑based markets. The launch of Project Vault , a new U.S. strategic mineral stockpile backed by more than $12 billion in public and private capital, aimed at securing materials across the entire value chain. Many minerals associated with our projects appear on the USGS critical minerals list, positioning Odyssey to operate in the same ecosystems that Project Vault is designed to fortify via long‑term procurement and supply stabilization. The United States and the Cook Islands announced a new strategic framework for critical minerals cooperation, including joint research, geological mapping, responsible investment, and downstream processing. Our ongoing scientific and exploration work in Cook Islands waters — including the deployment and upcoming recovery of ABML environmental monitoring systems — directly aligns with the framework’s pillars of transparent science, responsible governance, and partnership‑driven development. ​ Together, these policies initiatives and actions point to a clear trend: The U.S. and its allies are restructuring the global critical minerals landscape around security, transparency, and resilient supply chains. Odyssey’s proposed projects in the Cook Islands, Mexico, and the U.S. OCS are already operating in the regions, minerals, and scientific domains that this new policy architecture prioritizes. ​ We’re proud to contribute data, 30+ years of experience, technical / geological / environmental team, and science‑based exploration that support this emerging global framework. ​ More updates soon as this momentum continues. ​Disclaimer: The links provided on this page lead to third-party websites and media platforms. title: Introducing Discovery Campaigns for AppLovin advertisers AppLovin | Blog
summary: Introducing Discovery Campaigns for Axon Web Advertisers, a new campaign type driving purchases from entirely new customers who’ve never engaged your brand.
body_text: Earlier this year, we launched Prospecting Campaigns , a campaign type for e-commerce advertisers that optimizes for purchases from people who have never bought from you before. Advertisers responded quickly, with many seeing meaningful lifts in new customer ROAS and broad adoption across the platform. However, some advertisers asked a natural next question: what if I want to go even further and reach people who have never visited my site at all? Today, we're addressing that question with Discovery Campaigns. What Discovery Campaigns do differently Where Prospecting Campaigns focus on converting visitors who haven't purchased yet, Discovery Campaigns go even further: optimizing for purchases from people who have never interacted with your brand in any way. No site visit. No browse. No add to cart. Discovery is built to introduce entirely new audiences to your brand and convert them. AI optimizes. You choose what matters. At Axon, we believe AI should do what it does best: optimize toward a clearly defined goal. Our models are relentless at finding the right person, at the right time, with the right ad, doing so at a scale no manual process can match. But defining the goal is a business decision, not an algorithmic one. Different advertisers grow in different ways. A subscription brand may prioritize first-time purchasers. A marketplace may focus on reaching entirely new visitors. Another business may want to maximize total conversions regardless of customer status. There is no single “correct” objective. That is why we build campaign types around distinct definitions of success. Universal optimizes for total conversion performance. Prospecting focuses on new purchasers. Discovery goes one step further by optimizing for purchases from people who have never interacted with your brand at all. You decide what growth means for your business. We ensure the system pursues it as efficiently as possible. Getting started If you’re already running Prospecting Campaigns, you’re already set up. Discovery is built on the same foundation and uses the same historical purchase data. Simply select Discovery in Axon Ads Manager to launch a campaign that reaches entirely new audiences. If you’re not yet running Prospecting, share your historical purchase data in Ads Manager to get started. Shopify Shops are already covered through the app integration. Axon AI handles the rest. Early results Our initial alpha tests across a variety of brands showed very strong results. We’ve seen new visitor percentage more than double in many cases, and improve significantly in all of our initial test cases. This represents a meaningful shift toward acquiring customers who are entirely new to the brand. What's next Discovery Campaigns exist because advertisers asked for more control over how they grow. We're listening, and we're not done. Keep the feedback coming. When enough of you raise a need, we'll find a way to meet it.

This isn't just another connector; it is the meeting of two product philosophies that prioritize flexibility, code-based workflows, and data democratization. However, while data teams live in Lightdash, business stakeholders live in slide decks. Rollstack bridges that gap. This integration combines Lightdash’s modern, developer-friendly exploration with Rollstack’s ability to programmatically generate and update PowerPoint, Google Slides, Emails and Documents in a single click. (the “Company”, “Dream Finders Homes”, “Dream Finders” or “DFH”) (NYSE: DFH) announced its financial results for the fourth quarter and full year ended December 31, 2025. Fourth Quarter 2025 Highlights (As Compared to Fourth Quarter 2024) Homebuilding revenues of $1.2 billion compared to $1.5 billion Home closings of 2,536 compared to 3,008 Net sales increased 9% to repay a portion of the then outstanding balance under the revolving credit facility Total liquidity of $899 million as of December 31, 2025, comprised of cash and cash equivalents and availability under the revolving credit facility Return on participating equity of 15.3% compared to 29.7% Repurchased 1,832,865 Class A common shares for $41.8 million during the year ended December 31, 2025 Management Commentary Patrick Zalupski, Dream Finders Homes Chairman and CEO, said, “We pride ourselves on always being honest with our analysis of the business and the environment and clearly 2025 was a challenging year for the industry. We expect this difficult backdrop to continue for the homebuilding industry, but as we have stated previously, the best operators find a way to navigate any environment and there will always be winners and losers. Consistent with previous guidance, DFH will find a way to scale our business and I’m proud of the team’s ability to set annual Company records in both closings and net sales. Dream Finders finished the year with a positive fourth quarter, generating homebuilding revenues of $1.2 billion and delivering 2,536 closings, which allowed us to accomplish a Company record annual closings number of 8,608 homes. Our commitment to providing affordable homes was evident in our annual results. We spent over $100 million in mortgage buy-down programs, and provided homebuyers tailored sales incentives. These strategies proved effective as we increased net sales by 9% and 15% for the fourth quarter and full year, respectively, in a challenging macro-economic environment that significantly impacted consumer confidence. We plan to maintain our Company goal of delivering the highest possible value to our homebuyers and will continue to work hard to address affordability challenges that face the industry and our customers. In Q4 2025, we entered into a strategic partnership to acquire the Sawgrass Marriott Golf Resort & Spa in Ponte Vedra Beach, Florida, a 66-acre parcel adjacent to the renowned PLAYERS Stadium Course at TPC Sawgrass. This partnership provides opportunities to expand our lot pipeline and supports our future growth and profitability. This strategic venture will also benefit the local community by boosting tourism, creating jobs, and fostering a vibrant environment, positioning the Sawgrass Marriott as an important part of our future. We are very excited to own a meaningful portion of the partnership’s economics and believe this irreplaceable asset was acquired at an attractive price that will yield very successful long-term results for our shareholders. The ongoing complexity and difficulty of the housing sector persisted through 2025, yet our results demonstrate the strength and resiliency of our business, as well as the perseverance of our team in a challenging environment. I applaud the team for their effective execution amid choppy conditions and for their ongoing pursuit of new opportunities to drive value. As we look to 2026, we remain focused on further scaling our business and delivering long-term returns to our shareholders. We initiate our 2026 full year guidance of approximately 9,250 expected home closings.” Homebuilding Fourth Quarter 2025 Results Homebuilding revenues in the fourth quarter of 2025 were $1.2 billion, a decrease of 24% when compared to the fourth quarter of 2024. The decrease in revenues was driven by lower home closings and average selling prices (“ASP”). Declines in ASP across all segments were attributable to the continued use of sales incentives during the fourth quarter of 2025, as well as changes in our geographic product mix. The January 2025 Liberty Communities acquisition contributed 273 home closings with an ASP of $315,784 to the fourth quarter. Homebuilding gross margin percentage in the fourth quarter of 2025 was 16.7%, compared to 17.7% in the fourth quarter of 2024. The decrease in homebuilding gross margin percentage was primarily the result of higher sales incentives and land costs, as well as changes in product mix. Adjusted homebuilding gross margin in the fourth quarter of 2025 was 25.7%, compared to 26.9% in the fourth quarter 2024. Adjusted homebuilding gross margin is a non-GAAP financial measure. See “Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Financial Measures” below. Selling, general and administrative expense (“SG&A”) in the fourth quarter of 2025 increased 7% to $124 million, compared to $116 million in the fourth quarter of 2024. The increase in SG&A was primarily due to higher use of forward mortgage commitment programs, as well as expenses related to our increased community count, partially offset by lower compensation costs. SG&A as a percentage of homebuilding revenues in the fourth quarter of 2025 increased 310 bps to 10.7%, compared to 7.6% in the fourth quarter of 2024 due to absorption. Consolidated net income attributable to DFH in the fourth quarter of 2025 was $59 million, or $0.60 per basic share, compared to $129 million, or $1.35 per basic share in the fourth quarter of 2024. Net sales in the fourth quarter of 2025 were 1,756, an increase of 9% compared to 1,611 net sales for the fourth quarter of 2024. The cancellation rate in the fourth quarter of 2025 was 15.9%, an improvement of 290 bps compared with the fourth quarter of 2024 cancellation rate of 18.8%. The improvement in our metrics this quarter demonstrates our effective use of sales incentives and availability of high-quality, affordable homes within our markets. Adrian will join the executive leadership team and report directly to Mark Eubanks, president and chief executive officer. Adrian brings more than 30 years of global operational leadership experience to Brink’s. He began his career in Cardiff, Wales, as a mechanical engineering apprentice at the Royal Mint and went on to spend nearly two decades with General Electric. During his GE tenure, he held senior leadership roles across Aviation, Oil & Gas, and Industrial Solutions, managing multibillion dollar P&Ls, leading major supply chain transformations, and improving operational performance across multiple continents. Following GE, Adrian joined NCR Corporation, where he first led the $2.6 billion Hardware Group and later served as Executive Vice President of Service and Product. In that role, he oversaw a $5 billion P&L and a global team of more than 25,000 employees. His leadership significantly improved delivery, quality, and customer experience metrics while modernizing NCR’s global manufacturing and supply chain capabilities. Most recently, Adrian served as Senior Vice President of Operations at Carrier Corporation. He led an integrated global operations organization spanning manufacturing, supply chain, service, procurement, and logistics across more than 400 factories and distribution centers. Under his leadership, Carrier achieved significant cost savings, improved on-time delivery, and executed major strategic initiatives - including key acquisitions that expanded the company’s global footprint and accelerated growth in the commercial and datacenter segments. “Adrian is a worldclass operator with deep experience leading complex distributed service organizations through operational transformation,” said Brink’s president and chief executive officer Mark Eubanks. “His ability to strengthen execution, build high performing teams, and create customer centric operating models will be instrumental as we continue advancing our strong growth and profit expansion in North America and operational discipline across Brink’s.” “I’m honored to join Brink’s at such a pivotal moment,” said Button. “Brink’s has an incredible legacy and its AMS / DRS strategy provides a clear path for future growth. I look forward to partnering with our teams around the world to elevate operational excellence and strengthen the value we deliver to our customers.” About The Brink’s Company The Brink’s Company (NYSE:BCO), a leading global provider of cash and valuables management, digital retail solutions, and ATM managed services. title: How Rising Interest Rates Can Affect Your HELOC
summary: We’ll help you understand how rising interest rates affect your HELOC interest rates and what you can do to be prepared.
body_text: How Rising Interest Rates Can Affect Your HELOC If you’re a homeowner, interest rates are always top of mind. And if you have a Home Equity Line of Credit (HELOC) or are considering opening one, interest rates are even more important to understand and manage. At Landmark National Bank, we believe financial clarity leads to better outcomes. Below, we’ll help you understand how rising interest rates affect your HELOC interest rates and what you can do to be prepared. What Is a HELOC? A home equity line of credit, also known as HELOC is a second mortgage you can take out on your home that grants you a revolving line of credit. When you qualify for a HELOC, you will be granted a spending limit that you can borrow against as often as you need to. Your HELOC rate will be dependent on the value of your home and will come with variable interest rates. Many people use the funds from their HELOC for debt consolidation, home renovations, education/tuition, medical bills or the acquisition of another property. HELOCs are typically not used to fund everyday expenses. A HELOC differs from a traditional loan because it offers flexibility. Rather than receiving funds in one lump sum, a HELOC allows you to access money as you need it during the draw period. You can borrow, repay, and borrow again—similar to how a revolving line of credit works—while only paying interest on the amount you use. Most HELOCs are variable-rate loan products, which means your HELOC interest rate can change over time. This is one of the key differences between a HELOC and other types of home equity loans. Understanding HELOC interest rates and loan options: Variable-rate HELOC: With a home equity line of credit, interest rates fluctuate based on a benchmark index (often the prime rate), plus a margin set by the lender. When market rates rise or fall, your HELOC interest rate may change as well. Your interest rate is not fixed , it is variable making it the biggest differentiator between a traditional home loan. Fixed-rate home equity loan: With a fixed-rate loan, the interest rate stays the same for the life of the loan, and payments are predictable and not dependent on market variables. What Happens to Your HELOC When Interest Rates Rise? Variable rate HELOCs are more sensitive to rising interest rates, but also offer advantages and flexibility home owners need. When interest rates increase, the most noticeable change for HELOC borrowers is often the monthly payment. Here’s how rising interest rates can affect a HELOC: Your Interest Rate May Increase If your HELOC has a variable rate, an increase in the benchmark index (such as the prime rate) can cause your interest rate to rise. The timing and amount depend on the terms of your agreement. HELOC payment changes As interest rates increase, the interest portion of your payment also increases. This can result in higher monthly payments, especially if you’ve borrowed a significant portion of your available credit. Your overall borrowing cost can change Even small rate increases can add up over time. Understanding how rate changes affect your total interest paid can help you plan more effectively. It’s important to note that rate increases are typically incremental, not sudden or unpredictable. HELOC terms outline how often rates can change and whether there are caps on how high they can go. Rising interest rates don’t have to be overwhelming. At Landmark National Bank, our team helps you understand how HELOC payment changes affect your specific situation so you feel confident and informed no matter the situation. How Often Can HELOC Interest Rates Change? This is one of the most common questions homeowners ask. Most HELOC interest rates adjust monthly, based on changes to the underlying index. Your specific HELOC outlines these details, which is why reviewing your terms, or discussing them with a banker, can be helpful, especially during periods of rising interest rates. Your lending partner may include safeguards to protect against rising interest rates and HELOC payment changes. These include: Rate caps that limit how much the rate can increase at one time Lifetime caps that prevent the rate from exceeding a certain maximum Clear disclosures so you know what to expect If you have questions about your HELOC, a trusted banker can help you understand your terms so you stay in control of your finances. Why Rising Interest Rates Don’t Automatically Mean Trouble It’s natural to feel concerned when you hear about rising interest rates, especially if you have a variable-rate HELOC. But for many homeowners, a HELOC remains a flexible financial tool, acting as a reliable line of credit to manage large or unexpected expenses. Why a HELOC may work for you: You only pay interest on what you use You can borrow as needed, rather than taking a lump sum You maintain access to funds for ongoing or unexpected expenses You can repay and reborrow during the draw period Ways to Prepare for or Manage HELOC Rate Increases While you can’t control market interest rates, you can take steps to manage how rate changes affect your finances. Review your current HELOC balance Understanding how much you’ve borrowed, and how much remains available, helps you evaluate your exposure to rate changes. Build rate changes into your budget Planning for potential payment increases can reduce stress. Even setting aside a small buffer can help you stay confident if rates rise. Pay more than the minimum when possible Making additional principal payments can reduce your balance faster, which lowers the amount of interest you pay over time. Use your HELOC strategically HELOCs are often best used for long-term value investments, like home improvements, rather than everyday spending. Limiting your HELOC funds to these kinds of expenses can help you manage and pay down your loan. Talk with a banker about your options If you’re concerned about rising interest rates, work with a banking partner to understand alternatives, including fixed-rate options or repayment strategies. HELOCs vs. Other Borrowing Options in a Rising Rate Environment When interest rates rise, homeowners often compare HELOCs to other types of loans. Each option has its place, depending on your needs. HELOC: Flexible access to funds, variable rate, interest paid only on what you use Home equity loan: Fixed rate, predictable payments, lump-sum funding Personal loan: Fixed rate, shorter terms, typically higher interest rates Credit cards: Convenient but often carry significantly higher interest rates Real People, Real Access At Landmark National Bank, we believe in proactive conversations with our customers. Rising interest rates are a great reason to check in and ensure you are using your HELOC in the best way possible. Consider reaching out if: Your HELOC payment has changed and you want clarity You’re planning a major expense or renovation You’re nearing the end of your draw period You want to explore fixed-rate or refinancing options You want guidance in using your HELOC Bank Outside the Ordinary At Landmark, we believe banking should feel personal. We’re here to help you understand market situations and work through challenges. Together, we’ll decide if a HELOC is right for you or if another lending product is more beneficial. When interest rates change, we’re here to help you understand it can affect your HELOC, review your current terms and payment structure and ensure you have a loan that aligns with your goals. A HELOC remains a flexible, powerful tool for many homeowners. And with the right guidance, it can continue to work for you even in a changing rate environment. Thinking about opening a HELOC or adjusting to an existing one? Reach out today and let’s find a lending solution that works for you.

title: 4DMT Completes Enrollment in Gene Therapy Trial for Wet AMD
summary: Conexiant Vision: Delivering trusted clinical content, deep audience engagement, and educational resources for eye care professionals. Discover more through our magazines, newsletters, and events.
body_text: 4D Molecular Therapeutics announced that enrollment has been completed for 4FRONT-1 , a phase 3 clinical trial evaluating its investigational gene therapy, 4D-150, in patients with wet age-related macular degeneration. The multicenter, randomized, double-masked study enrolled treatment-naïve patients at more than 100 sites across North America and was completed in approximately 11 months, according to the company. 4FRONT-1 is comparing a single intravitreal injection of 4D-150 with aflibercept 2 mg (Eylea; Regeneron) administered every 8 weeks. The primary endpoint is noninferiority in mean change from baseline in best-corrected visual acuity at 52 weeks. A key secondary endpoint is reduction in treatment burden, measured by the number of aflibercept injections required in the 4D-150 arm compared with the control arm. Patients in both groups may receive supplemental aflibercept as needed. The trial is part of a broader registrational program that includes a second phase 3 study, 4FRONT-2 , which is enrolling both treatment-naïve and recently diagnosed treatment-experienced patients globally. Enrollment for 4FRONT-2 is expected to conclude in the second half of 2026. 4D-150 uses an intravitreal adeno-associated virus vector to deliver genes encoding aflibercept and an anti–VEGF-C component, with the goal of providing sustained intraocular anti-VEGF expression. Top-line data from 4FRONT-1 are expected in the first half of 2027, the company said in a press release. RP

title: No Credit Check Loans (Canada): Full Guide to Alternative Lending Options (2026)

body_text: No-credit-check loans in Canada are financial products that provide immediate access to funds without requiring traditional credit score verification, offering Canadians with poor credit or limited credit history an alternative path to emergency financing. TLDR - Quick Summary No credit check loans include payday loans, cash advance services , installment loans, and Buy Now Pay Later services — you can apply online and get approved without a hard credit check Interest rates range from 0% (cash advance apps like Bree) to the federal maximum of $14 per $100 borrowed for payday loans in Canada, which works out to roughly 365% APR Loan amounts typically range from $100 to $5,000, depending on the product type and lender Approval process can take just a few minutes, with many lenders offering same-day funding via e-transfer No credit impact during the loan application process — most lenders use a soft credit check or no credit check at all, though missed payments may still be reported Provincial regulations vary, with stronger consumer protections now in place across Canada following the January 2025 federal lending reforms Red flags include upfront fees, unlicensed payday lenders, and interest rates exceeding legal limits What Are No-Credit-Check Loans in Canada? No-credit-check loans in Canada represent a diverse category of financial products designed to serve borrowers who cannot access traditional banks due to credit history limitations, providing immediate funding without the extensive credit verification processes typically required by mainstream financial institutions. These alternative lending solutions have become increasingly sophisticated, encompassing everything from traditional payday loans to innovative cash advance apps that offer interest-free funding options. With roughly 34% of Canadians incurring at least one NSF fee per year — often because their account is just a few dollars short — many Canadians turn to no-credit-check loan options to bridge short-term cash flow gaps and avoid costly bank fees. Modern no-credit-check lending has evolved significantly beyond the stereotypical storefront payday loan model, now encompassing digital-first platforms like Bree that offer interest-free cash advances of up to $750 with no credit check required, transparent fee structures, and consumer-friendly repayment terms. Many Canadians qualify even if they receive income through government benefits like Employment Insurance (EI), Canada Pension Plan (CPP), Canada Child Benefit (CCB), or provincial programs like ODSP and Ontario Works. How Do They Work? No-credit-check loans work through streamlined loan application processes that prioritize speed and accessibility while maintaining responsible lending standards through alternative risk assessment methods. Borrowers typically complete online applications within just a few minutes, providing basic personal information, employment details, and banking information that enables most lenders to verify income and assess financial stability without accessing traditional credit reports. It's worth understanding what "no credit check" actually means. Most lenders in this space perform a soft credit check — a background verification that doesn't appear on your credit report or affect your credit score. This is different from the hard credit check that traditional financial institutions use, which can temporarily lower your score. Some lenders, including cash advance apps, skip credit bureaus entirely and rely only on your bank account activity and income deposits to determine eligibility. The underwriting process relies heavily on bank account analysis, examining transaction patterns, income regularity, and account balance history to evaluate a borrower's ability to repay the loan. This approach means that even Canadians with a poor credit score, no credit profile, or those who have gone through a consumer proposal can still qualify based on their current financial situation. Once approved, funding is typically delivered through Interac e-transfer or direct deposit, often within hours of completing the loan application. Repayment arrangements vary by product type, with payday loans requiring full repayment on the next payday, while installment loans offer monthly payments spread over a longer period. Cash advance apps align repayment with borrowers' regular pay periods and next paycheque. For those seeking instant access to funds without interest charges, platforms like Bree represent the evolution of this lending model, offering cash advances up to $750 with zero interest, no credit checks, and flexible repayment options aligned with your next payday. You can borrow what you need and repay within up to 90 days — far longer than the typical payday loan window. What are the Types of No Credit Loans in Canada? Credit check loans in Canada encompass four distinct categories, each serving specific consumer needs and financial emergencies through unique product structures and repayment mechanisms. Online Payday Loans remain the most traditional form of no-credit-check lending, offering short-term loan funding typically ranging from $100 to $1,500, with repayment due on the borrower's next payday or next paycheque. As of January 2025, these products are subject to a federal cost cap of $14 per $100 borrowed across all provinces with approved payday loan regimes, along with comprehensive consumer protections, including cooling-off periods and rollover prohibitions. Payday lenders in provinces like Ontario and Nova Scotia must also comply with additional provincial requirements. Cash Advance Applications represent the newest evolution in no-credit-check lending, with innovative platforms offering interest-free funding up to $750 through mobile applications. These services, including Bree , have transformed the market by eliminating interest charges while providing fast access to emergency funds aligned with borrowers' payroll schedules. You can apply online in a few minutes, and many Canadians get approved and funded the same day. Installment Loans bridge the gap between short-term payday products and traditional loan options, offering larger loan amounts ranging from $300 to $5,000 with flexible repayment terms extending from several months to multiple years. These loans work well for borrowers who need to borrow a larger amount and prefer predictable monthly payments. Buy Now Pay Later Services enable consumers to split purchase costs into multiple payments, typically offering four equal installments over six weeks or longer payment plans for larger purchases, without requiring credit checks for smaller amounts. Interest Rates and Fees Breakdown Interest rates and fees for no-credit-check loans in Canada vary significantly depending on the product type and lender, with recent regulatory changes leading to more consumer-friendly pricing structures across the alternative lending market. Cash Advance Apps like Bree offer 0% interest rates on cash advances up to $750, representing the most cost-effective option for Canadian borrowers seeking short-term funding without traditional credit verification. These platforms may charge small convenience fees for expedited funding but maintain transparent pricing structures without hidden fees. Unlike payday lenders, cash advance apps like Bree also charge zero late fees — so if you need a bit more time to repay, you won't face penalties. Online Payday Loans are subject to federal and provincial regulations that cap costs at $14 per $100 borrowed in most jurisdictions, translating to approximately 365% APR for typical two-week loan terms. While expensive, these rates are lower than historical payday lending costs and include consumer protections. Keep in mind that if you can't repay on time, many lenders will attempt to withdraw funds from your bank account automatically — and if the money isn't there, you could face NSF charges on top of any loan fees. Currently, most Canadian banks charge $45 to $48 per NSF transaction, though as of March 12, 2026, NSF fees on personal accounts will be capped at $10 under new federal regulations. Installment Loans typically feature APRs ranging from 19.99% to 35%, depending on loan amounts and borrower qualifications. Since January 2025, the federal criminal interest rate has been set at 35% APR for consumer lending products, which means any lender charging more than this on a non-exempt loan is operating illegally. Longer repayment terms reduce individual payment amounts while spreading costs over extended periods. BNPL Services generally offer interest-free payment plans with standard terms, accompanied by late fees ranging from $8 to $25 per missed payment, making them cost-effective for consumers who maintain consistent payment schedules. No-credit-check loans offer significant benefits for Canadian borrowers who cannot access traditional banking products, while also presenting potential drawbacks that require careful consideration. Pros include: Immediate access to funding without credit score requirements Fast approval process and funding processes, often within hours No impact on credit rating during loan application Available to borrowers with bad credit or limited credit history Flexible qualification requirements focusing on income rather than poor credit Options like Bree offer interest-free funding up to $750 Cons include: Higher costs compared to traditional bank products Limited loan amounts for most products Short repayment terms that may create cash flow pressure Potential for debt cycling if not managed responsibly Less comprehensive consumer protections than traditional lending What are the Red Flags to Avoid? Canadian borrowers should be vigilant about identifying potentially predatory or illegal lending practices that may target vulnerable consumers seeking no-credit-check funding options. Major red flags include: Requests for upfront fees before loan approval — this is illegal in Canada, and legitimate lenders never ask you to pay before you're approved Interest rates exceeding provincial or federal legal limits — since January 2025, the criminal interest rate is 35% APR for most consumer loans, with payday loans capped at $14 per $100 Unlicensed lenders operating without proper regulatory oversight — always verify a lender's licence through your provincial consumer affairs office before you apply online Guaranteed approval claims regardless of financial circumstances — no legitimate lender can guarantee approval without reviewing your finances Pressure tactics during the application or collection process Unclear fee structures or hidden fees buried in the loan agreement Requests for unusual collateral or direct access to your government benefits Legitimate lenders like Bree maintain transparent pricing structures, proper licensing, clear loan agreement terms and conditions, and customer service support that helps borrowers understand their obligations and rights. What are Some No-credit-check Loan Options? Payday Loans Payday loans in Canada continue to serve Canadian borrowers seeking immediate short-term loan funding, with companies offering online payday applications with same-day funding capabilities. These products typically provide $100 to $1,500 with repayment due on the next payday, subject to provincial cost limits of $14 per $100 borrowed. Modern payday lenders have embraced digital transformation, offering 24/7 online applications, instant decision algorithms, and funding through Interac e-transfer within 30 minutes of approval. Despite their higher costs, payday loans remain valuable for borrowers who need immediate funding and cannot access other alternatives, particularly in provinces like Nova Scotia, where regulations ensure consumer protection. Cash Advance Cash advance applications represent the most consumer-friendly evolution in no-credit-check lending, with platforms like Bree offering interest-free cash advances of up to $750, along with transparent fee structures and flexible repayment options. These innovative platforms focus on income verification and bank account analysis to provide fast access to emergency funds without the high-interest debt associated with traditional payday lending. The interest-free model, combined with user-friendly mobile applications and educational resources, represents the future direction of responsible alternative lending. Buy Now, Pay Later BNPL services have expanded rapidly across Canadian retail markets, with providers offering payment flexibility for purchases ranging from everyday items to major expenses. These services typically divide purchase amounts into four equal installments over six weeks, with no interest charges for on-time payments. The BNPL market in Canada is projected to reach $7.5 billion by 2025, reflecting growing consumer demand for flexible repayment options that offer transparency and avoid traditional credit requirements. Installment Loans Online installment loans cater to borrowers who need larger amounts with manageable monthly payments, typically ranging from $300 to $5,000, with repayment terms of several months to several years. These products provide APRs up to 32%, representing a middle ground between payday loans and traditional bank lending. These products appeal to borrowers who need larger amounts of funding for debt consolidation, home repairs, or major purchases and prefer predictable repayment schedules to single-payment loans. Auto Title Loans Auto title loans remain available in some Canadian provinces, allowing borrowers to use their vehicle titles as collateral for larger loans typically ranging from $1,000 to $10,000. These products require borrowers to own their vehicles outright and provide physical titles as collateral, with repayment terms typically set to extend by 30 days and offering renewal options. While title loans can provide larger amounts than unsecured alternatives, borrowers risk losing their vehicles if they cannot repay, making these products suitable only for borrowers confident in their repayment ability. Credit Building Tips No-credit-check loans can serve as stepping stones toward improved financial health when used strategically alongside broader credit-building initiatives that help borrowers transition to more affordable traditional lending products. Effective credit-building strategies include: Obtaining secured credit cards that report to credit bureaus Making consistent loan payments on all existing obligations Keeping credit utilization below 30% on any existing credit products Monitoring credit reports regularly for errors or improvements Considering credit-builder loans from credit unions Using services like Bree responsibly to avoid expensive borrowing while building financial stability The key to successful credit building involves establishing consistent payment patterns while gradually increasing credit account diversity and maintaining low credit balances relative to available credit limits. Scam Prevention Guide Protecting yourself from lending scams requires understanding common predatory tactics while recognizing the characteristics of legitimate lending operations that prioritize consumer protection and regulatory compliance. Scam prevention strategies include: Verifying lender licensing through provincial regulatory databases Avoiding lenders that request upfront fees or unusual personal information Researching companies through the Better Business Bureau and consumer review platforms Understanding provincial lending cost limits and reporting violations Choosing regulated alternatives like Bree that maintain transparent operations and customer support Reading all the loan agreement terms and conditions before signing Legitimate lenders maintain professional customer service, provide clear documentation, hold proper licensing, and offer pricing structures that comply with provincial regulations. FAQs Are no-credit-check loans legal in Canada? ‍ Yes, credit check loans are legal across Canada when provided by licensed lenders operating within provincial regulatory frameworks that include cost caps, consumer protections, and operational standards. What's the average credit score in Canada? ‍ The average Canadian credit score is approximately 650-700, with scores above 700 considered good and scores below 600 creating challenges for traditional loan approval. What's the maximum interest rate allowed? ‍ Maximum interest rates vary by province and product type, with payday loans capped at $14 per $100 borrowed in most jurisdictions and the federal criminal interest rate set at 47% APR for most lending products. Can I get approved with bankruptcy? ‍ Many no-credit-check lenders will approve borrowers with previous bankruptcies , focusing on current income and financial stability rather than past credit difficulties, though recent bankruptcies may limit options. How quickly can I get funds? ‍ Funding timelines vary from minutes to 24 hours, depending on the lender and delivery method, with platforms like Bree offering same-day funding for approved applications. Do these loans help build credit? ‍ Most no-credit-check loans do not report positive payment history to credit bureaus; however, missed payments may be reported, which can be neutral to credit monitoring unless the account is mismanaged. What happens if I miss payments? ‍ Missed loan payments may result in late fees, NSF charges, and potential reporting to collection agencies, though specific consequences vary by lender and provincial regulations. What credit score is required for a $ 5,000 personal loan? ‍ Traditional banks typically require credit scores above 650 for $5,000 personal loans, while no-credit-check installment loan providers focus on income verification rather than credit scores. In a Nutshell Loans in Canada provide essential financial services for millions of Canadians who cannot access traditional banking products, offering everything from interest-free cash advances through platforms like Bree to comprehensive installment loan solutions for larger financial needs. While these products carry higher costs than traditional bank lending, provincial regulations ensure consumer protection through cost caps, operational standards, and comprehensive disclosure requirements. Success with no-credit-check lending requires careful product selection, responsible borrowing practices, and integration with broader financial wellness strategies that help borrowers build toward more affordable traditional lending options over time.
